numbers.evidence: Abstract: "We introduce a web-scale dataset for time-continual pretraining of LLMs derived from 114 dumps of Common Crawl (CC) ... We also design time-stratified evaluations".

Table 1 (flights, 2M): "Time .026±.001" for DUN. App. E.2.2: "We report computation time for a single batch of size 512, which we evaluate across 5 runs." The figure is the time for a batch of 512 points, not per prediction.

Table 1 (flights, 2M): "TCE .087±.009" for DUN (Dropout .096±.017, Ensemble .090±.008). Sec. 4.3: "DUNs present superior uncertainty calibration. This allows them to achieve the best LL, tied with Ensembles and Dropout."

note: TCE in the paper is "Tail Calibration Error" (calibration of the 10% and 90% intervals), not "total calibration error"; the value .087±.009 is DUN's TCE, better than Dropout and Ensembles but worse than MFVI (.068) and SGD (.084). Flights: "we train on the first 2M data points and test on the subsequent 100k." Time .026 is per batch of 512 (CPU), so 'per prediction' misstates the unit.

"Currently, our database contains 91,763 crystal structures, more than 10,000 computationally derived properties (ion-transport data), and 121 properties obtained from literature".

note: 91,763 and 91,688 are database counts. The paper does not say the full CAVD+BVSE->NEB funnel ran over all 91,763 structures; the screening it reports starts from the 21,542 Li/Na candidates, and it reports preliminary data for 7,678 structures (geometric analysis) and 12,000 BVSE activation energies. 'Running the full funnel over 91,763 structures' overstates the scope, but the counts themselves are correct. CAVD = crystal structure analysis by Voronoi decomposition; BVSE = bond valence site energy, as stated.
